Today's headlines:

  • OpenAI details low-latency voice stack — OpenAI published an unusually concrete engineering look at how it rebuilt its WebRTC path for real-time voice AI, focusing on turn-taking, latency, and global scale.
  • Cerebras tracks toward major IPO — The AI chip company, closely tied to OpenAI workloads, is reportedly heading for a blockbuster IPO that could test investor appetite for non-Nvidia AI infrastructure plays.
  • Sierra raises $950 million — Bret Taylor’s enterprise AI startup now has over $1 billion to spend, underscoring how aggressively capital is concentrating around application-layer incumbency plays.
  • OpenAI and Anthropic push deeper into enterprise services — Both companies are launching joint ventures with asset managers to package and sell enterprise AI more directly, hinting at a services-heavy go-to-market shift.
  • Image AI launches outperform chatbot upgrades in app growth — New app-store data suggests visual generation features drive far stronger download spikes than incremental chatbot improvements, though monetization remains weak.
  • Harvard study finds AI beat doctors on some ER diagnoses — A new medical study reports that at least one large model outperformed two physicians on emergency-room diagnostic cases, adding evidence for AI as a clinical second reader.
  • DoorDash rolls out merchant AI tooling — DoorDash added AI for merchant onboarding, menu-photo enhancement, and website generation, a practical example of vertical AI quietly changing SMB operations.
  • Roomba founder returns with a companion robot — Colin Angle’s new startup unveiled a dog-sized robotic companion, a notable signal that consumer robotics may be re-opening as multimodal AI makes behavior feel less scripted.
2026-05-04.title: Briefing — May 4, 2026
